article_title: A comparative study of student performance in all-ceramic crown preparation by clinical-phase students.

A., Shubayr Mosa A., Nandalur Kulashekar Reddy. (2025). A comparative study of student performance in all-ceramic crown preparation by clinical-phase students. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07512-0
title: 39-point analytic rubric for all-ceramic crown preparation assessment
description: A grid-style analytic rubric scoring all-ceramic crown preparation on a 39-point scale: tooth preparation (25 points across occlusal reduction, axial reduction, taper, margin placement, and finishing on 5-point scales), tissue management (5 points), final impression (5 points), and time management (4 points). The article states the weighting "ensures alignment with clinical priorities while maintaining granularity in assessment". It was developed via Delphi-style consensus, pilot testing, and calibration to >85% agreement, achieving κ of 0.52–0.78 and ICC of 0.65–0.89 across domains.
requirements: Two trained, calibrated evaluators scoring independently with blinding of student identities
Prior student training on the rubric parameters and criteria before the exam
constraints: Developed for a single institution with gender-separated clinics; the article notes its generalizability may be affected but states its criteria align with international prosthodontic standards
examples: Used in a double-blinded final clinical exam for 72 fifth-year students, scored independently by two faculty evaluators
